finding.claim: Path traversal in /dl lets an unauthenticated remote attacker read arbitrary files on the host (e.g. /dl?f=../../../../etc/passwd), because the user-supplied name is joined to root with no confinement check.
finding.source: files.go:12 - r.URL.Query().Get("f"), attacker-controlled query parameter, no authentication required
finding.sink: files.go:13 - os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(root, name)); file contents returned to the client at files.go:18 via w.Write(data)

trace.note: /dl is registered with no auth or middleware wrapper
name taken verbatim from the f query parameter
filepath.Join('/srv/files', '../../../../etc/passwd') lexically cleans to '/etc/passwd', escaping root
file bytes written to the HTTP response

finding.guards_checked: No prefix check after Clean (filepath.Clean+strings.HasPrefix absent); no filepath.EvalSymlinks; no os.Root confinement; no allowlist of filenames or extensions; no auth on the route; error path only returns 404 and does not block a successful read. filepath.Join does not discard root for absolute input (/etc/passwd becomes /srv/files/etc/passwd), so only '..' sequences are exploitable. Precondition: the service is reachable on :8082 (files.go:34 binds all interfaces).

verdict.guard_found: none. /dl is registered bare at files.go:32 with no auth or middleware. The name comes straight from the query at files.go:12 and goes into filepath.Join at files.go:13, which Clean-s the '..' segments, so '/srv/files/../../../../etc/passwd' resolves to '/etc/passwd'. There is no prefix check, EvalSymlinks, os.Root, or allowlist. The error path (files.go:14-16) only returns 404 and does not block a successful read. The bytes are written at files.go:18. Binding to ':8082' at files.go:34 exposes it on all interfaces.
verdict.reason: Every trace line matches the code: the unauthenticated /dl route (files.go:32) takes the raw query value (files.go:12), filepath.Join cleans the '..' segments to escape /srv/files (files.go:13), and the file contents are returned (files.go:18), with no guard between the attacker and the read; the only remaining uncertainty is deployment reachability, which the bind at files.go:34 supports.

finding.claim: The /dl handler has no authentication or authorization check, so anyone who can reach port 8082 can download any file under /srv/files, including files that may be intended to be private to other users.
finding.source: files.go:12 - unauthenticated request to /dl with any f value naming a file under root
finding.sink: files.go:13 and files.go:18 - os.ReadFile of the requested file and its return to the client

trace.note: /dl registered on the default mux with no auth middleware
handler performs no identity, session, or ownership check
requested file chosen solely by the client
contents returned without any per-file access decision

finding.guards_checked: No auth middleware, no session or token validation, no per-user or per-file ownership check, no rate limiting. The listener is plaintext HTTP on all interfaces (files.go:34), so the file contents are also exposed on the wire. This finding is independent of F1: it applies to any file a client names, even without traversal.

verdict.guard_found: none. files.go:32 registers /dl on the default mux with no middleware. The handler at files.go:11-19 has no identity, session, token, or ownership check, and no rate limiting exists. The only branch is the os.ReadFile error path (files.go:14-16), which returns NotFound and is not an access control.
verdict.reason: Every trace line checks out: /dl is registered unauthenticated at files.go:32, the client-chosen name is read at files.go:12, the file is read at files.go:13, and the contents are written back at files.go:18 with no access decision, and the listener is plaintext on all interfaces at files.go:34. The attacker is anonymous and network-reachable, and the claim that anyone reaching :8082 can read any file the server can open is accurate, though whether those files are actually "private" is an assumption the code does not establish.
